title: Artificial Intelligence and Polycrisis Resilience
subtitle: Emerging Technologies and the Future of Global Risk Reduction
description: A foundational monograph examining how artificial intelligence and emerging technologies can be developed, diffused, and applied to reduce human and systemic…
contribution: Establishes the conceptual architecture for integrating Artificial Intelligence into Polycrisis Resilience—originated by Hunter Hughes, Founder of H Heuristics—connecting Risk Anticipation, Technology Diffusion, Sustainable Development, and Institutional Capacity across four 21st-century horizons (2026–2035, 2035–2050, 2050–2075, and 2075–2100).
abstract:
Artificial Intelligence and Polycrisis Resilience is a foundational publication within the H Heuristics Polycrisis Resilience Series, based on the concept developed by Hunter Hughes, Founder of H Heuristics (https://polycrisisresilience.hheuristics.com/).
It answers the central research question of how artificial intelligence and emerging technologies can be developed, diffused, and applied to reduce human and systemic vulnerability to the global polycrisis across four analytical horizons (2026–2035, 2035–2050, 2050–2075, and 2075–2100).

keyFindings.title: Artificial intelligence is a potentially transformative enabling technology for Polycrisis Resilience, but its contribution to global risk reduction depends not merely on frontier computational capabilities—it depends on how equitably AI is distributed, governed, and integrated into sustainable development.

AI strengthens resilience through four core channels: Risk Anticipation (forecasting and early warning), Technology Diffusion (access and productivity), Sustainable Development (energy and resource efficiency), and Institutional Capacity (planning and cross-system coordination).

AI simultaneously introduces systemic risks—unequal access, compute and talent concentration, electricity and water strain, infrastructure dependencies, cybersecurity threats, and labor disruption—that can widen global vulnerability unless proactively governed.

Deploying equitable, energy-efficient AI across early warning (12.4x BCR), smart grids (10.8x), epidemic surveillance (10.5x), and precision agriculture (9.9x) compresses global vulnerability from 65.0 (2025) to 25.0 by 2050 and 11.0 by 2100 (-83.1%).
